[[Hellhound]]s can be assigned as a [[slayer task]] at 65 combat level by various [[Slayer masters]]. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular hellhounds only attack with their fairly accurate [[melee]] bites; it is recommended to either [[safespot]] them or keep [[Protect from Melee]] on at all times. Hellhounds are primarily known for their high drop rate of [[clue scroll (hard)|hard clue scrolls]], at a rate of 1/64, or 1/32 if killing in the [[Wilderness]] with a [[Ring of wealth (i)|imbued ring of wealth]]. They also drop [[ensouled hellhound head]]s and the [[smouldering stone]].

Outside of the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the [[Stronghold Slayer Cave]] for general slayer, as there are four rooms of three or four hellhounds in each one, and a [[dwarf multicannon]] can be set up in their caves. They may also be killed in the [[Catacombs of Kourend]] for [[ancient shard]]s and [[dark totem]] pieces. The catacombs do not allow for a cannon, but is a [[Multicombat area]] and allows for relative AFK training, especially with a [[Venator bow]], and is also quite close to the entrance. Once the aggression timer expires, the player can simply run south and up the vine to the [[Giants' Den]] to reset aggression. Some players opt to restore prayer at an altar and teleport back to this location using [[Xeric's talisman]]'s Xeric's Heart option or the [[Kourend Castle Teleport]] spell (requires 48 [[Magic]] and completion of [[Client of Kourend]] to unlock the spell).

In the [[Wilderness]], hellhounds are primarily killed in the [[Wilderness Slayer Cave]], with a group of five slightly stronger hellhounds in a multicombat area. The drop rate of the smouldering stone from these hellhounds is increased by 50%, and they have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table, which can help offset some supply costs. However, the cave itself is a very popular [[player killing]] hotspot despite the hellhounds being below level 20 Wilderness, and players killing them here should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose. These hellhounds are generally killed if assigned by [[Krystilia]].

[[Revenant hellhound]]s '''do not''' count towards a normal hellhound task, despite being ghostly hellhounds.

Alternatives for normal hellhounds include the [[Skeleton Hellhound (Calvar'ion)|skeleton]] [[Skeleton Hellhound (Vet'ion)|hellhounds]] summoned by [[Calvar'ion]]/[[Vet'ion]] respectively. While the main boss itself is obviously not a hellhound, players can progress through the task with the boss' spawns and make reasonable profit at the same time. Every boss kill will spawn four hellhounds in total, two pre-enrage and another two post-enrage. However, the bosses are also popular player killing hotspots and players should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose. 

A final alternative is [[Cerberus]] for players who have 91 [[Slayer]] or higher, with a minimum of 86 with a [[wild pie]] boost. Cerberus is much stronger than other hellhounds, with additional mechanics, and a chance at valuable unique drops. It is recommended that a player has access to the [[Ward of Arceuus]] spell and either an [[Arclight]], [[Emberlight]], or [[Scythe of Vitur]] to kill Cerberus, as worse setups may offer considerably less (or even negative) profit. This is due to her summoned souls attack (which drains up to 90 prayer, reduced to 60 with Ward of Arceuus, if successfully prayed against) resulting in higher than expected usage of prayer potions.

[[Ensouled hellhound head]]s can be sent to the [[bank]] with a charged [[Soul bearer]], or resummoned on the spot for additional prayer experience.

==Exceptions==
*[[Revenant hellhound]]s cannot be slain for a Hellhound Slayer task. They can only be slain for a [[Revenants|Revenant]] Slayer task, which can be assigned by [[Krystilia]].
*The [[Skeleton Hellhound]] fought during the [[In Search of the Myreque]] [[quest]] counts towards a Hellhound Slayer task during the quest. However, refighting it in the [[Nightmare Zone]] later on does not count towards a task.
*[[Bouncer]] fought during the [[Fight Arena]] [[quest]] counts towards a Hellhound Slayer task during the quest. However, refighting it in the [[Nightmare Zone]] later on does not count towards a task.
*[[Bouncer (ghost)|Bouncer's ghost]] fought during [[The General's Shadow]] [[miniquest]] does not count toward Hellhound Slayer tasks. Regardless, it cannot be fought after the completion of the miniquest.

==Safespots==
[[Safespotting]] can be done with [[Ranged]], [[Magic]], [[halberd]], or a [[salamander]]. In the [[Catacombs of Kourend]], ensure you stand on the eastern side of the hallway, otherwise a hellhound can enter and attack. The other safespots are completely safe from the hellhounds entering. The Wilderness safespot is still below level 20 wilderness, so is safe to teleport out of when player killers arrive.

Since they occupy a large space of 2-by-2 squares, hellhounds can easily be safespotted in [[Taverley Dungeon]] on rocks and columns, or in the [[Witchaven Dungeon]]. In the [[Karuulm Slayer Dungeon]], they can be safespotted with range at the entrance by staying against the north wall and luring the two northern spawn Hellhounds towards the entrance. They may also be safespotted in the Kourend dungeon by ranging them from the south of the room, using the corner of the entry hallway to block. Also it is possible to safespot them from the south in the Kourend Catacombs from the north exit, drag them along the wall and safespot them from the furthest tile in the corridor to the brutal dragons. It is also possible to safespot Hellhounds in the [[Wilderness Slayer dungeon]] by running to the gap in the stalagmites on the eastern wall in level 21 Wilderness. Get the closest Hellhound to the north from that spot to be aggressive towards you and use it to block others from attacking until the aggression timer is up, after which then safespot can be used freely.
